submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 gave the best observed signal efficiency at the allocated Level-1 rate in the simulation scan. Around the optimum, repeated 100k-event emulations gave about 92.6% average efficiency at 34 GeV, higher than nearby L2 points (~92.3% at 33 GeV, ~92.1% at 32 GeV) and clearly above the best observed Algorithm-L1 (~86%) and Algorithm-L3 (~74%) performance. The 34 GeV threshold is within the allowed 20--60 GeV range. Important caveat: the available project documents do not provide a Level-1 FPGA latency number for any candidate, so the 4.0 us hard latency requirement is not verified from the provided evidence and must be signed off before implementation/freeze.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: The rate allocation document gives 8 kHz. The simulation tool reports signal efficiency at the allocated rate; a scan over the three listed algorithms and thresholds 20--60 GeV showed Algorithm-L2 highest. Repeated runs near the maximum gave ~92.6% average at 34 GeV, exceeding Algorithm-L1 (~86% best observed) and Algorithm-L3 (~74% best observed).

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Algorithm-L2 as one of the candidate algorithms: iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: No provided project document or simulation output gives Level-1 FPGA latency for Algorithm-L2 or the other candidates. candidate_specs.md only states that all candidates fit FPGA resource budgets, which does not establish latency.
Recommended threshold is 34.0 GeV, within the allowed 20--60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L2 at 34.0 GeV.
